blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — El Niño is expected to bring hotter days and water shortages, but these conditions may have another consequence for public health: a greater risk of dengue transmission. In Central Visayas, where dengue infections have more than doubled from last year, health officials are pointing to warmer temperatures, humidity, and changing household water practices as factors that may favor the spread of the disease. Dengue is a viral infection transmitted through the bite of infected Aedes aegypti mosquitoes, which commonly thrive in warm, humid tropical environments, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).
